shapeprojector:blockdesc-projector-*: A surveyor's instrument of the old world. Once calibrated, the Jonastech Shape Projector casts a luminous guide onto the ground — circles, rings, and figures of exact measure — so that walls and waterways may be laid true. It builds nothing itself. It only shows you where.

shapeprojector:handbook-projector-center:
Every figure the instrument casts shares one center: the projector's own position, moved by an offset along each horizontal axis in steps of half a block.

An offset of 0, 0 sets the center on the projector itself — a single block at the heart, and so an odd diameter. An offset of 0.5, 0.5 sets it on a block corner — four blocks share the middle, an even diameter. An offset of 0.5, 0 sets it on an edge, for a middle two blocks wide and one deep.

Larger offsets — 12.5 and −3, say — set the center away from the instrument altogether: in open water, in air, inside a wall already standing. The projector need not occupy the center of what it measures; it may stand beside the work. The dial shows the resolved center, and a small marker of its own is cast upon it so the alignment can be read at a glance.
shapeprojector:handbook-projector-layers:
One projector holds an ordered list of layers. Each layer is a figure of its own — a circle, a ring, an ellipse, a rectangle, a regular polygon, or a spiral — and all of them share the projector's center. Each carries its own measurements, a height offset relative to the projector, a color, and a switch to set it aside without discarding it. Layers may be added, removed, duplicated, and moved up or down the list.

Each layer also carries a thickness and a height. A thickness above one widens the line inward from its outer edge, so a single layer can mark a band three blocks broad rather than three layers set one apart. A height above one repeats the figure on that many levels going up from the layer’s own offset, so a single layer can describe a whole wall instead of one course each. In Follow terrain the height is counted from each column’s own ground, so a wall of even height rises over uneven land. A thickness equal to the radius makes the figure solid — a disc, a filled square — and a layer set to fill up to its level also marks every block from the ground beneath it up to that level, so a pit under a platform shows the very fill it needs.

The projector’s marks may be made fainter or bolder, and may be put out altogether while the small model above the instrument keeps showing every figure; the model may also be made to show the ground, buildings and waters around the projector, each block in its own colour, so that the plan sits inside a miniature of the place.

A mark is a guide only. It has no substance and no collision; blocks placed upon it stand where it stood, and a mark whose place is already filled by a solid block turns green, so the figure completes before your eyes as you build. The number of layers one instrument may hold is set by the server (forty-eight, unless changed).
shapeprojector:handbook-projector-vertic: Two ways of standing: Fixed Y and Follow terrain

A level outline laid across sloping ground is half buried and half afloat. Each layer therefore stands in one of two ways.

Fixed Y draws the outline at the projector's own height plus the layer's offset, wherever the ground may be. This is for level work — wall tops, floors, platforms. Where the earth swallows the mark, cut down to it; where the mark hangs in air, fill up to it. That, too, is information.

Follow terrain sets each column of the outline on the surface — one block above the highest solid block beneath it — plus the layer's offset, if any. The outline lies upon the land like a rope laid out by hand: the moat's dig line, the hillside path, the fence line. As the ground is excavated the mark follows down into the pit, always marking the present floor's edge. Treat fluid as surface governs water: on, the mark rests on the water's top and shows the bank; off, it looks through the water to the bed and shows the bottom. Columns whose land is not yet loaded stand at Fixed Y until it is.

Circles, rings and spirals begin in Follow terrain, being usually of the landscape; rectangles and polygons begin in Fixed Y, being usually of the building. Either may be changed on any layer.
shapeprojector:handbook-projector-exampl:
Set the projector at the center of a round holding and give it three layers.

Layer one: a ring, inner radius 20, outer radius 23, in Follow terrain. This is the moat — three blocks wide — and its two lines lie on the land wherever the land goes. Dig between them; as the pit deepens the lines follow the floor down, and the edge is never lost.

Layer two: a circle, radius 11, in Follow terrain. This is the path that rings the house, resting on whatever ground it crosses.

Layer three: a circle, radius 30, in Fixed Y with a height offset of the wall's intended top. This is the wall top, level all the way round — hanging in air where the ground falls away, buried where it rises. Build up to it.

Three figures, one center, concentric by construction. Nothing was counted.

The projections may be hidden for yourself alone with the Toggle shape projections key; other players see them still.
shapeprojector:msg-noaccess: You may not adjust this projector here.
shapeprojector:gui-layer-limit: This projector holds at most {0} layers.
shapeprojector:info-layer-more: … and {0} more layers ({1} in all) — right-click to see them
shapeprojector:chat-preset-skipped: [Shape Projector] {0} malformed preset(s) were skipped (kept in the file).
shapeprojector:gui-tip-add: Adds a fresh default layer — circle, radius 11, Follow terrain — at the end of the list and selects it. Layers: {0} → {1} (limit {2}).
shapeprojector:gui-tip-add-full: Unavailable: this projector already holds its limit of {0} layers.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-remove: Deletes layer {0} and selects the nearest one left. Layers: {1} → {2}.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-remove-last: Unavailable: a projector always keeps at least one layer.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-duplicate: Inserts an exact copy of layer {0} ({1}) directly below it and selects the copy. Nothing is resized or moved — same size, same Y offset {2}. Use it as the starting point before editing.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-move: Swaps layer {0} with layer {1}. List order only: every setting, Y offset included, travels with its layer, so nothing in the world moves.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-move-first: Unavailable: layer {0} is already at the top of the list.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-move-last: Unavailable: layer {0} is already at the bottom of the list.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-addup:
Copies layer {0} and lifts the copy one block, then selects the copy.
Y offset {1} → {2}. The size is untouched ({3}).
Each press adds the next course, so thirty presses give a thirty-block tower.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-addout-spiral: Unavailable for a spiral: there is no single radius to step. A spiral's size comes from its turns, spacing and start radius.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-global-clamped: {0} already at the minimum would stay put.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-math-ring: Inner and outer radius both {0}, so the gap between the two circles keeps its width
shapeprojector:gui-tip-math-rectangle: Width and depth both {0} — one block on each of the four sides
shapeprojector:gui-tip-math-spiral: A spiral has no radius to step, so it is skipped.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-math-clamped: but {0} is already the smallest this shape allows, so the layer would stay exactly as it is.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-radius: Distance from the center out to the outline, in half-block steps. One circle, one line: radius 11 draws a hoop 23 blocks across. The inside is left empty, and how broad the line itself is comes from the Thickness field below — for two separate circles with a gap between them, choose the Ring shape instead.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-innerradius: A Ring draws TWO circles around one center, and this is the smaller of them. The blocks between the two are not marked — that empty band is the moat or path you dig. Must be smaller than the outer radius, and leave at least 1.5 between them or the two lines touch and read as one band. If one line is all you want, switch the shape to Circle, which has a single Radius.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-outerradius: The larger of the Ring's two circles. Outer minus inner is how wide the untouched band between them is: 20 and 23 mark out a three-block moat. Closer than 1.5 apart and the two lines meet. Both radii always move together, so Add layer out and Global radius keep that width.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-radiusx: Half-width of the ellipse along X (east–west), in half-block steps.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-radiusz: Half-depth of the ellipse along Z (north–south), in half-block steps. Set it equal to Radius X and the ellipse becomes a plain circle.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-width:
Full outside width along X (east–west), in whole blocks, edge to edge.
A rectangle can only sit exactly on center when the side matches the center: an odd side for a whole-number offset, an even side for a .5 one. A mismatch is rounded OUTWARD by one block — the Drawn size line below always shows what you really get.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-depth: Full outside depth along Z (north–south), in whole blocks, edge to edge. Same odd/even rule as Width, and the Drawn size line below shows the size actually marked.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-sides: How many equal sides, three or more. Three is the Triangle entry in the shape list; the more sides, the closer the figure comes to a circle.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-circumradiu: Distance from the center to a CORNER — not to the middle of a side, which falls closer in. A hexagon of circumradius 11 has corners 11 blocks out and side-middles about 9.5 blocks out.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-rotation: Turns the figure about its center, in degrees. At 0 the first corner points due east; the others follow it clockwise seen from above. A square at 45° becomes a diamond.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-turns: How many complete laps the spiral makes. Fractions are allowed: 2.5 stops half way round the third lap.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-spacing: How far the spiral steps outward per lap, in blocks — the gap between one lap and the next. The outermost radius comes to start radius + spacing × turns.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-startradius: Radius the spiral begins at. 0 starts it on the center itself.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-param-direction: Which way the spiral winds as it goes outward, seen from above with north at the top.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-layerlist: Which layer the settings below belong to. Every entry shows its number, shape and size, and says so when it is switched off.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-shape: The figure this layer marks out. The fields below change to match it. Triangle is simply a regular polygon with three sides.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-yoffset:
This layer's height, in blocks.
In Fixed Y it counts from the projector block: +3 marks three blocks above it, −2 two below.
In Follow terrain it counts from the ground the outline lands on: 0 lies on the surface, +1 hovers one block over it.
Add layer up is exactly this field +1 on a copy of the layer.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-verticalmode:
Fixed Y marks one dead-level height whatever the ground does — wall tops, floors, platforms. Where earth swallows the line, dig down to it; where it hangs in air, build up to it.
Follow terrain drops every block of the outline onto the surface below it and follows the floor down as you excavate — dig lines, hillside paths, fence lines.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-fluid: Follow terrain only. On, the outline rests on the water's surface and marks the bank. Off, it looks through the water to the bed and marks the bottom.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-buildfeedback: Marks whose block has already been filled with something solid turn green, so the figure completes in front of you as you build.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-color: Colour of this layer's marks, in the world and in the miniature above the projector. Every entry in the list shows its colour beside its code. Give crossing layers different colours to tell them apart where they overlap. The done-tint green is not offered — that colour means "already built".
shapeprojector:gui-tip-color-hex: For an exact colour: type it as #RRGGBB (or #RGB). The square on the right always shows the colour currently chosen, whether it came from the list or from here; a typed colour appears at the top of the list as a custom entry.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-enabled: Hides this layer without deleting it: its settings are kept, and Global radius still adjusts it, so a hidden layer never falls out of step with the rest.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-projenabled: The projector's master switch. Off, it marks nothing at all and every layer keeps its settings.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-offsetx:
Moves the shared center east (+) or west (−) of the projector, in half-block steps. Every layer uses this one center.
A whole number sets the center on a block, giving an odd diameter; a .5 sets it on the seam between blocks, giving an even one.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-offsetz: Moves the shared center south (+) or north (−) of the projector, in half-block steps. Same half-step rule as Offset X. Large offsets are fine — the projector may stand well to one side of the figure it marks.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-center: The world coordinates every layer is drawn around: the projector's own position plus the offsets below.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-preset-name: Name to save the current setup under. Typing over an existing name overwrites that preset.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-preset-list: Your saved setups. Presets are stored per player, not per projector, so they follow you to any projector you can edit.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-preset-save: Saves every layer and the center offset under the name typed to the left. An existing name is overwritten. Presets are your own and are kept between worlds.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-preset-delete: Deletes the preset chosen above. The projector's own layers are left alone.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-preset-loadreplac: Discards this projector's layers and puts the preset's layers in their place, its center offset included. Applies at once — it does not wait for Apply.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-preset-loadappend: Keeps the layers already here and adds the preset's layers after them; the center offset stays as it is. Anything past the {0}-layer limit is dropped and reported below the toolbar. Applies at once — it does not wait for Apply.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-apply: Sends everything in this dialog to the server, which checks it and updates the projection for every player. Edits made here take effect only when you press this.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-close: Closes the dialog. Anything edited since the last Apply is discarded.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-holoenabled: Shows or hides the small floating model above the projector, on its own. The marks out in the world are not affected — that is the World marks switch below (and Projector on above turns off both). The setting belongs to this projector and every player sees the same thing; to hide every projection for yourself alone, use the Toggle shape projections key instead.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-holofigures: Shows or hides the figures inside the small model above the projector. Off, with Model surroundings on, the model is a survey of the land alone — ground, buildings and water with no plan drawn on it. The marks out in the world are not affected.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-worldmarks: Shows or hides the full-size marks out in the world, on its own. Off, the projector is hologram-only: the small model above it keeps showing every figure while nothing is drawn on the ground. The setting belongs to this projector and every player sees the same thing.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-opacity: How solid the marks out in the world look, from {0} (barely there) to 100 (opaque). {1} is the original look. Only the world marks follow this; the hologram keeps its own contrast so it stays readable whatever you choose here.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-terrainmap: On, the small model above the projector also shows what is already standing around it — ground, walls, pits, buildings and water, each block in its real colour — with the coloured figures drawn in their true places among it: a model of your home and of the work at once. Hologram only; nothing grey is ever drawn out in the world, whether the world marks are on or off.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-terrainmap-radius: How far out from the projector the surroundings are modelled, in blocks each way (up to {0}). Up to 64 the model is block-exact; beyond that it samples every 2nd, 3rd or 4th column and draws each as a wider tile, so a big radius reads as a coarser survey rather than a slower one.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-terrainmap-height: How far above and below the projector the surroundings are modelled, in blocks (up to {0}). Blocks outside that window are left out of the model.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-fill-fixed:
Besides the figure at its own Y offset, marks every block from the ground up to that level under each column of the figure — so a pit under a platform shows exactly the fill it needs, and a solid figure (thickness up to the radius) becomes a whole raised floor. The ground rises as you fill, so the fill marks vanish as they are done; the level itself keeps the build feedback.
With the fluid rule off the fill starts at the lake bed — a causeway.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-fill-drape:
Besides the figure on the ground, marks every block from each column's ground up to the HIGHEST ground under the figure — levelling the whole figure up to its highest point. As you fill, the ground rises and the marks vanish; note that building ABOVE the highest point raises the level with it, as any Follow terrain figure climbs — use Fixed Y to pin the level.
With the fluid rule off the fill starts at the lake bed.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-fluid-fill: Fill up to level, Fixed Y. On, water counts as ground and the fill starts on the water's surface. Off, the fill starts at the bed under the water — mark out a causeway or a filled pond.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-thickness:
How many blocks wide the marked line is, from 1 up to {0} for this figure — at {0} the figure is solid: a disc, a filled square, a filled polygon.
Thickness grows INWARD: the outer edge stays exactly where the radius puts it and the band eats toward the center, so a circle of radius 11 and thickness 3 is a band running from about 9 out to 11. One layer at thickness 3 replaces three separate layers at radius 9, 10 and 11.
A spiral thickens by repeating its own path at smaller start radii, which widens the track the same way.
shapeprojector:gui-tip-height:
How many blocks tall this layer stands, from 1 upward. The same outline is marked on that many levels going UP from the layer's Y offset, so one layer describes a wall that would otherwise need one layer per course.
In Follow terrain each column is measured from its own ground, so a tall draped layer keeps its height over a slope instead of levelling out.
Build feedback checks every level separately, so a half-built wall greens as far up as it is finished.
